title: Randomized Stability Orchestrator and CI Perf Gates for Prefill/Decode Scheduling
creator: Anita Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a randomized stability orchestration layer for the benchmarking harness that (1) generates diverse synthetic input matrices reflecting real traffic distributions, (2) exercises kernel selection and attention optimization branches under stochastic pacing of prefill and decode, and (3) plugs into CI as deterministic perf gates with noise-aware thresholds. Motivation: existing golden-baseline runs are brittle to small upstream scheduler or kernel changes; we need a complementary strategy that surfaces regressions which only show under randomized concurrency mixes or corner attention windows.

Scope and deliverables:
- Randomized workload generator: a corpus synthesizer that samples from empirically-derived distributions (sequence length, prompt prefix entropy, batch size mix, kv-cache hit rates). Generator supports deterministic seed mode and 'fuzzy' mode for daily stochastic sweeps.
- Matrix-driven scenario catalog: a small set (15) of seed matrices that target known risk vectors (very long prefill + short decode, many short prefill requests with high overlap, attention window ramp-ups, low-batch high-concurrency tails). Each matrix includes metadata tags to route runs to specific kernel-selection code paths.
- Stability orchestrator: runner that schedules thousands of micro-runs across available kernel variants, quantization profiles, and attention-optimized codepaths and collects per-run telemetry with trace IDs and SLO-relevant metrics (p50/p90/p99 latency, cpu/gpu occupancy, memory high-water marks, kv cache hit).
- CI integration: new perf gate job type that runs a fixed deterministic seed suite on every release branch and an extended randomized sweep nightly. Perf gates support adaptive thresholds: for deterministic seeds thresholds are tight; for randomized sweeps thresholds are statistical (e.g., 98% of runs must be within X% of baseline).
- Regression detection and triage: automated signal detector that uses bootstrapped confidence intervals to flag true regressions vs noise; creates triage issues with top-correlated telemetry (kernel variant, sequence-length bucket, prefill/decode ratio).

Non-goals: replacing existing golden baselines or synthetic canonical workloads. This is complementary: find regressions that deterministic golden baselines miss and provide higher signal for scheduling-related degradations.

Success criteria:
- Nightly randomized sweep runs complete within budgeted cloud hours and produce reproducible summaries.
- CI deterministic gate fails only for real regressions with <5% false-positive rate over 4 weeks.
- Developer time-to-root-cause for scheduler-attention regressions reduced by 30% through richer telemetry and seeded repros.

Architecture notes and important trade-offs:
- Deterministic seeds are cheaper to reason about, but risk missing rare interactions; fuzzy sweeps increase coverage but add flakiness — we mitigate with statistical gating and seed capture for failing shards.
- We capture heavy telemetry per-run; storage cost controlled by configurable retention and by uploading sampled traces for failing or borderline runs only.
- To avoid CI runtime explosion, nightly randomized sweep targets a representative subset; full exhaustive matrix runs are scheduled to a monthly 'deep-sweep' job.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/RS-7643-randomized-stability-orch (draft)
- Prototype runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-perf/compare/feature/randomized-orch (PR #412)
comments: 2025-02-14 - Anita K: Kickoff with runtime and bench teams. Identified seed distribution sources: production telemetry samples (sanitized), historical golden-run corpus, and synthetic anomaly catalog.

2025-02-19 - Marco V: Prototype seed sampler completed. Initial corpus derived from 200k anonymized traces across hosted + dedicated deployments. Observed a heavy tail of short-prefill/long-decode combos where current kernels fall back to slower code path.
2025-02-22 - Priya Desai (SRE): We should ensure nightly sweeps run in a separate quota/project to avoid noisy neighbor effects on production benchmarks. Added as dependency.

2025-02-25 - Marco V: Implemented deterministic-seed mode and matrix metadata tagging. Ran local 5k-run sweep against kernel-v1/v2 and saw an exposed 12% p99 regression in kernel-v2 for the 'short-prefill-high-overlap' matrix. Captured seeds and added seed-lock ticket ENG-57203.
2025-02-27 - Design review (Leah M): UX request to surface failing seeds in Console rollouts dashboard so PMs can correlate regressions with recent rollouts.

2025-03-01 - Engineering sync: Decided statistical gate thresholds: nightly-sweep requires 95th percentile of p99-latency ratio to be <= 1.10 relative to golden baseline with bootstrap CI. Deterministic gate uses absolute p99 < baseline * 1.03. Added follow-up to formalize thresholds (ENG-57207).
2025-03-02 - Marco V: Opened PR #412 with runner and CI job definitions. Requesting review from perf infra (Danny) and SRE (Priya).
